## Sikhae (식해) – A Spicy, Fresh‑Seafood “Cold Stew” Sikhae is a classic Korean dish that looks like a stew but is actually a **marinated raw‑fish salad**. It’s served cold (or at room temperature) and is perfect for a quick, refreshing meal or a side dish at a Korean barbecue. > **Why it’s called a “stew”** > The name comes from the Korean word *hae* (해) meaning “to boil.” Historically, the dish was cooked briefly in a hot pot, but modern versions simply marinate the seafood in a spicy sauce, so it’s more of a “marinated raw fish” than a true stew. --- ### 1. Ingredients | Category | Item | Approx. Amount | Notes | |----------|------|----------------|-------| | **Seafood** | Tuna (or yellowtail) | 200 g | Fresh, sashimi‑grade | | | Salmon | 200 g | Fresh, sashimi‑grade | | | Shrimp (peeled, deveined) | 150 g | Fresh or frozen, thawed | | | Squid (cleaned, sliced) | 150 g | Fresh | | | Scallops | 100 g | Fresh | | | Optional: octopus, mussels, clams | 100 g | Add for variety | | **Vegetables** | Cucumber | ½ | Thinly sliced | | | Red onion | ¼ | Thinly sliced | | | Green onion | 2 stalks | Chopped | | | Radish (optional) | 50 g | Thinly sliced | | | Kimchi (optional) | 50 g | Adds tang | | **Sauce** | Gochujang (Korean red pepper paste) | 2 Tbsp | Adjust to taste | | | Gochugaru (red pepper flakes) | 1 Tbsp | Optional, for extra heat | | | Soy sauce | 1 Tbsp | Low‑sodium if possible | | | Rice vinegar | 1 Tbsp | Adds acidity | | | Sesame oil | 1 tsp | For aroma | | | Sugar or honey | 1 tsp | Balances heat | | | Garlic (minced) | 1 clove | | | | Ginger (minced) | ½ tsp | | | | Sesame seeds | 1 tsp | Toasted | | | Optional: lime juice | ½ tsp | Adds brightness | | **Optional Garnish** | Pickled radish | 1 Tbsp | For crunch | | | Fresh cilantro | 1 tsp | | > **Tip:** Use only sashimi‑grade fish. If you’re unsure, ask your fishmonger for “sashimi” or “sashimi‑grade” fish. --- ### 2. Preparation Steps | Step | Action | Time | |------|--------|------| | **1. Prep the seafood** | • Cut tuna, salmon, and other fish into bite‑size cubes (≈1 cm).
• Slice shrimp, squid, scallops into thin strips.
• Keep everything chilled until you’re ready to mix. | 10 min | | **2. Slice vegetables** | • Thinly slice cucumber, red onion, radish (if using).
• Chop green onions. | 5 min | | **3. Make the sauce** | In a bowl, whisk together:
• Gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, sugar, minced garlic, ginger, and sesame seeds.
• Add lime juice if you like a citrusy kick. | 5 min | | **4. Combine** | • In a large mixing bowl, add all the seafood and vegetables.
• Pour the sauce over the mixture.
• Toss gently but thoroughly so every piece is coated. | 5 min | | **5. Marinate** | • Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a lid.
• Refrigerate for **at least 30 minutes** (up to 2 hours) to let flavors meld. | 30 min–2 h | | **6. Serve** | • Transfer to a serving dish.
• Garnish with chopped green onions, toasted sesame seeds, and optional pickled radish or cilantro.
• Serve immediately, or keep chilled until ready to eat. | 5 min | > **Serving suggestion:** > - Pair with steamed rice and a side of *kimchi* or *pajeon* (green‑onion pancake). > - For a Korean BBQ spread, place the sikhae on a platter next to grilled meats and let guests spoon it onto their plates. --- ### 3. Variations & Tips | Variation | How to Do It | |-----------|--------------| | **Add a touch of sweetness** | Replace sugar with honey or a splash of maple syrup. | | **Make it milder** | Reduce gochujang and gochugaru; add more soy sauce and vinegar. | | **Add a protein boost** | Toss in a handful of edamame or tofu cubes. | | **Make it vegan** | Use only vegetables (e.g., mushrooms, tofu, seaweed) and omit fish. | | **Make it a “hot” version** | Add a splash of hot sauce or a pinch of cayenne pepper. | > **Safety note:** > - Keep all raw seafood refrigerated at 0–4 °C until you’re ready to mix. > - If you’re using frozen seafood, thaw it in the fridge overnight or under cold running water. > - Wash your hands and all surfaces thoroughly after handling raw fish. --- ### 4. Quick Reference (Recipe Card) ``` Sikhae (식해) – Spicy Raw‑Fish Salad Ingredients: - 200 g tuna (sashimi‑grade) - 200 g salmon (sashimi‑grade) - 150 g shrimp, peeled - 150 g squid, sliced - 100 g scallops - ½ cucumber, thinly sliced - ¼ red onion, thinly sliced - 2 green onions, chopped - 2 Tbsp gochujang - 1 Tbsp gochugaru (optional) - 1 Tbsp soy sauce - 1 Tbsp rice vinegar - 1 tsp sesame oil - 1 tsp sugar - 1 garlic clove, minced - ½ tsp ginger, minced - 1 tsp toasted sesame seeds - Optional: ½ tsp lime juice, 1 Tbsp pickled radish Method: 1. Cube fish, slice shrimp/squid, keep chilled. 2. Slice veggies, chop green onions. 3. Whisk sauce ingredients together. 4. Toss seafood + veggies + sauce in a bowl. 5. Marinate 30 min–2 h in fridge. 6. Garnish and serve cold. Enjoy a fresh, spicy, Korean “stew” that’s ready in under an hour!``` --- **Enjoy your homemade sikhae!** If you have any questions about ingredient substitutions or want to tweak the heat level, just let me know. Happy cooking!
